name: The Baltimore Sun editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates The Baltimore Sun Center (low confidence, Oct. 2026) and Ad Fontes rates it Middle. Largest Maryland daily, bought in January 2024 by Sinclair executive chairman David Smith with Armstrong Williams; Williams said that month the Sun 'will stop endorsing political candidates' (Baltimore Banner, Jan. 20, 2024). Its opinion pages have run guest pieces against Question 3, but no board position was found, and no Sun editorial on Baltimore City Questions A to I was found (the site blocks automated reads).

name: The Baltimore Banner
lean_basis: Nonprofit newsroom founded 2022. Publishes a full 2026 voter guide and candidate profiles; as a 501(c)(3) it does not endorse candidates or ballot questions.

name: The Washington Post editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates The Washington Post Editorial Board Lean Right (1.0, just past Center) after reviews in July and August 2026, with low confidence; it rates the Post's news pages Lean Left. In February 2025 owner Jeff Bezos refocused the opinion section on 'personal liberties and free markets.' Its editorial page (The Post's View) shows no endorsements in DC or Maryland races from Sept. 26 to Oct. 17, 2026, so it is treated as not endorsing this year. No policy statement on local endorsements was found.

name: League of Women Voters of Maryland (VOTE411)
lean_basis: Nonpartisan. Does not endorse candidates; publishes candidate questionnaire answers on VOTE411 and may take positions on ballot questions after member study.

name: Maryland Democratic Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization; backs its nominees and campaigns for Question 3 (chair Steuart Pittman).

name: Maryland Republican Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization; backs its nominees. Runs the 'Save Our Voice' campaign to defeat Question 3.

name: Maryland State and DC AFL-CIO
lean_basis: State labor federation. Its Labor Votes site campaigns FOR Question 1; its 2026 slate (Airtable embed) endorses mostly Democrats, including Moore.

name: Maryland State Education Association
lean_basis: State teachers union (NEA affiliate); endorses mostly Democrats. Listed among Moore's 2026 endorsers.

name: Maryland Chamber of Commerce
lean_basis: Statewide business lobby. Takes positions on fiscal ballot questions; candidate endorsements run through its PAC. 2026 positions not found.

name: Maryland League of Conservation Voters
lean_basis: Environmental advocacy group; endorses candidates (nearly all Democrats) and scores legislators. Listed among Moore's 2026 endorsers.

name: Planned Parenthood Maryland Action Fund
lean_basis: Reproductive-rights advocacy arm; endorses candidates who support abortion access, nearly all Democrats.

name: Maryland Right to Life PAC
lean_basis: Anti-abortion advocacy group; endorses candidates opposed to abortion, nearly all Republicans.

name: NRA Political Victory Fund
lean_basis: Gun-rights PAC; grades candidates A through F and endorses the higher-graded candidate, nearly always a Republican.

name: Maryland State Fraternal Order of Police
lean_basis: Statewide police union. Splits its 2026 ticket: endorsed Democrat Wes Moore for governor (per Moore's campaign) and Republican Jim Rutledge for attorney general (Sept 8, 2026).
